biography: Pedro Guilherme, a name whispered with both excitement and frustration in the Formula Dirt paddock, hails from the sun-drenched favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His journey began not on the pristine circuits of Europe, but on the treacherous, makeshift dirt tracks carved into the hills surrounding his neighborhood. Racing wasn't a hobby; it was an escape, a way to prove himself against the odds. Pedro's raw talent was undeniable, catching the eye of a local mechanic who cobbled together a rudimentary kart, fueling Pedro's early ambitions. He clawed his way through regional championships, his aggressive driving style turning heads and ruffling feathers. A defining moment came at the Brazilian National Dirt Championship where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he stormed through the field to snatch victory on the final lap, securing his place in Formula Dirt. Now, at 34, the fire seems to flicker inconsistently. Moments of brilliance are often overshadowed by unforced errors and questionable decisions, leaving many wondering if the boy from the favelas can reignite the spark that once burned so brightly.
drivingStyle: Guilherme's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the limits of grip and leaving little margin for error. Tire management is not his forte; he prefers to attack from the outset, sacrificing longevity for immediate gains. Under pressure, Guilherme can either elevate his performance to unbelievable heights or crumble spectacularly, making him an unpredictable force on the track.

careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian National Dirt Championship in 2014 after starting last due to a mechanical issue, demonstrating an incredible display of skill and determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the World Dirt Championship in 2019, costing him a potential world title and severely damaging his reputation.
